options: A data member that is declared const so it can never change after construction
A condition that is checked only inside the constructor and never again later
A condition on the object's state that holds whenever control is outside its members
A global variable shared by all instances so that they stay mutually consistent
questions.explanation: The constructor establishes the invariant and every public operation preserves it.

questions.prompt: A joint with vmax = 3 rad/s is at q = 0.4 rad. What is the smallest dt in seconds for which a move to 1.3 rad is accepted? Give a number with 2 decimals.
A validator is written 'if (q < lo || q > hi) reject;'. What happens with q = NaN?
options: It is rejected, because NaN is out of range
It is accepted, because both comparisons are false
questions.explanation: All ordered comparisons with NaN are false; write !(lo <= q && q <= hi) or test std::isfinite first.

questions.prompt: Which accessor design lets callers break the invariant of a private member q_?
options: const double& position() const { return q_; }
questions.explanation: A non-const reference to private state is a public write door that skips validation.

questions.prompt: A P controller with kp = 3 and dt = 0.05 drives q toward a target. The update is q += kp*(target-q)*dt. Starting at q = 0 with target 2, what is the position after one step? Give a number with 2 decimals.
double run(Controller c) { return c.compute(1); } is called with a PController object. What is the problem?
options: The argument is sliced to its Controller part, so derived behavior is lost
Nothing is wrong; virtual dispatch still reaches PController::compute on the copy
The destructor of the argument runs twice because of the by-value copy
The call is ambiguous because both classes define a compute member
questions.explanation: Polymorphic types must be passed by reference or pointer.
